key_insight: Revisiting local feature matching with a data-driven lens—scaling training data and standardizing evaluation—substantially improves matching accuracy and downstream 3D reconstruction, narrowing the gap with modern feed‑forward 3D models.
problem_solved: Local feature matching has stagnated due to small, fragmented training sets and inconsistent evaluation protocols; this work addresses the lack of large-scale data and rigorous benchmarks that prevent progress and fair comparison.
method: Assemble and scale diverse, task-focused datasets for local feature matching to unlock data-driven improvements.
Adapt training objectives and model design to leverage larger data (robust matching losses, contrastive/matching supervision, and architecture refinements).
Provide standardized evaluation and benchmarks across SfM and reconstruction tasks to measure real-world impact and comparability.
impact: Makes local feature matching more robust and competitive, improving SfM, localization and 3D reconstruction pipelines for practitioners; establishes a reproducible benchmark and training paradigm for future research.
